records.subsystem: HLE / NID-to-name diagnostic table
behavior_sources: PSP NID derivation rule NID = SHA-1(export_name)[0:4] little-endian, as implemented by pspdev psp-build-exports (S)
PSPSDK header identifier corpus (S)

ind1_outcome.step_a: Removed the 8 sentinel entries after proving consumer behavior: sr_nid_name() has exactly two consumers, both fprintf(stderr) diagnostics in hle.c reached only when no handler is registered, both NULL-tolerant, and both print the raw NID regardless. Import resolution never touches the table. import_audit_gate reports the same 371 registrations before and after, and none of the 8 appear in HST's import set.
ind1_outcome.step_b: Every retained entry now carries an evidence class in tools/nid_corpus.json: pspsdk-sourced 840, hash-verified 623, library-attributed 54, editorial-alias 10, unresolved 88.
ind1_outcome.step_c: The NID is recomputed from the name at generation time for all 1463 derivable entries, so their numeric constants are physically absent from the tracked corpus. Only the 152 NIDs that genuinely cannot be derived are stored, and they now stand as the explicit visible residue. A test asserts that a derivable entry storing a NID is an error.
ind1_outcome.step_d: The 54 library-attributed, 10 alias and 88 unresolved entries were retained. Failing the derivation rule means unproven, not wrong.
ind1_outcome.phase_e: tools/gen_nidnames.py no longer reads a PPSSPP checkout; the tracked corpus is its only input.
ind1_outcome.classification_unchanged: Still derived-data. The name list remains PPSSPP-suggested and no independence is claimed for it. What changed is how much is copied, not where the names came from.

uncertainty: SCOPE OF THE VERIFICATION. For a verified entry the claim is exactly: given the name, the NID is independently reproducible factual data. It does NOT establish independent provenance of the NAME LIST, originality of the surrounding table structure, correctness of the unverified entries, or absence of PPSSPP influence. 623 of the 1463 verified names were suggested by PPSSPP's tables and have no second source; only 840 are also regenerable from PSPSDK headers.

AN UNVERIFIED ENTRY IS NOT A WRONG ENTRY. Ten alternative derivations were tested against all 160 (big-endian prefix, other digest windows, trailing NUL, case variants, MD5, and library-prefixed names). None explained a single entry. The negative result means these names are neither confirmed nor refuted, not that they are incorrect.

The 54 library-attributed entries have the shape <Library>_<own NID in hex>. An earlier draft of this audit called them zero-information; that was wrong. The export name is unknown, but the entry does record which library owns the NID (sceUtility 9, sceImpose 5, sceMpeg 5, scePower 5, and 16 further libraries), and the bare hex the diagnostic prints does not carry that. They are retained.

The 10 editorial aliases are firmware-range suffixes on a base name that is itself present and verifiable in the same table (sceKernelSetCompiledSdkVersion at 0x7591c7db, scePowerSetClockFrequency). They are almost certainly not export names, but the NIDs they label are real. Retained and flagged.

The 8 sentinel entries (0x13370001, 0xc0de0001-3, 0x756e6e6f, 0x756e6f00, 0x756e6f10, 0xdeadbeaf) carry reserved __ identifiers and/or NID values no digest realistically produces; 0xc0de0001-0003 are sequentially allocated across three related names, which a hash cannot do. High confidence these are emulator-internal identifiers rather than firmware exports. This is a structural inference from the numeric shape, not a proof about PSP firmware.

The 88 unresolved names cluster as 71 sceNp*, 6 sceNet*, 6 sceKernel*, and 5 stragglers. The sceNp concentration is consistent with those libraries using another derivation, but no tested hypothesis confirms it.

TRAP: any identifier hashes to some 32-bit value. The PSPSDK header corpus produced 617 sce*/psp* tokens absent from the table, overwhelmingly SDK-internal helpers that are not firmware exports. The corpus may only CONFIRM a pair already believed real; it must never mint new entries.

findings.title: NOTICE.md's per-file derivation inventory is incomplete and contradicts several file headers
findings.detail: Measured across tracked src/ C/C++ sources: 11 files declare 'Derived from PPSSPP' and 15 declare 'Derived from sal063/PSP-recompilation-project'. NOTICE.md's derived-module table names 9 paths in 6 rows, all attributed to PPSSPP. Three distinct defects follow. (1) UNDER-COVERAGE, PPSSPP: evf.h, gpu_sdl3vk/ge_gpu.c, recomp.c, recomp.h and savedata.c declare PPSSPP derivation in-file but are absent from the table. (2) NO PER-FILE sal063 INVENTORY AT ALL: NOTICE covers sal063 only as prose under 'Project lineage' ('began as a fork of this toolkit and retains substantially modified pipeline/runtime code'), so 15 files carrying a sal063 derivation notice have no per-file record anywhere, an asymmetry with how PPSSPP is treated. (3) DIRECT CONTRADICTIONS: ge_shared.h's header declares sal063 while NOTICE attributes it to PPSSPP Core/GE; audio.c's header declares sal063 while NOTICE attributes it to PPSSPP sceSasCore.cpp and Core/Audio, and the file body cites neither upstream anywhere. Issue #103 closed with an acceptance criterion requiring that NOTICE.md, file headers and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES not contradict one another; that criterion is not currently met.
findings.action: ADDRESSED 2026-08-06 by IND-6, by ADDING to NOTICE.md and changing no file header. (1) evf.h, gpu_sdl3vk/ge_gpu.c, recomp.c, recomp.h and savedata.c are now in the PPSSPP table. (2) a per-file sal063 inventory now exists. (3) ge_shared.h is documented as a CHAIN -- both attributions correct at different levels -- and audio.c is explicitly marked unresolved in NOTICE.md itself, retaining its PPSSPP attribution while recording that sal063's own CREDITS.md does not list it. The remaining question needs a PPSSPP source comparison and stays open.

findings.title: RESOLVED 2026-08-06: sal063 derivation headers are accurate and under-state the inheritance
findings.detail: The prior text speculated that the sal063 headers might be boilerplate, on the grounds that h264_mf.c drives Windows Media Foundation and so had 'no plausible counterpart in a PSP recompilation toolkit', and that sched.c's architecture implied low retention. IND-4 measured it against the public upstream at da17b0e and BOTH HYPOTHESES WERE WRONG. h264_mf.c retains 89.7% of an upstream file that already existed; sched.c retains 79.8%; osk_win.c, iso.h, ge_shared.h and interp.h are at 100%. Across 44 common source files, 11310 of sal063's 13482 normalized code lines are still present (83.9%), and 40.1% of the current code in those files is shared with sal063. Retaining the attribution was correct; the stated reason for doubting it was not.
findings.action: Superseded by docs/provenance/SAL063_RETENTION_2026-08-06.md. The remaining open question is narrower and needs a PPSSPP comparison: whether the retained portions carry PPSSPP expression directly or only sal063's re-expression of it.

findings.title: recomp.c overstates current derivation of the VFPU transcendental kernels
findings.detail: src/rt/recomp.c:949 calls the kernels 'exact ports of PPSSPP's table-based kernels'. The 2026-08-05 PSP-3001 capture shows they diverge from PPSSPP on six of eight transcendentals and that hardware agrees with Nakagawa on all eight. The comment is factually stale.
findings.action: Correct the comment to state the origin AND the divergence AND the hardware backing. Do not delete the derivation statement; the kernels' structure and the tables they index still originate upstream.

findings.title: No development history exists for the period in which derivation occurred
findings.detail: The repository's first commit 7ac90b2 (2026-07-19, 'Moving to GitHub') is a squashed import in which every runtime file appears fully formed. There is no reachable pre-import history on any ref. Git therefore cannot corroborate or refute any file-level derivation claim about the original runtime, in either direction. This is a distinct problem from #102's 'history contains material it should not': here the relevant history is absent.
findings.action: Record this limitation wherever a provenance claim is made. It is also the strongest single reason the project must never assert clean-room status.

findings.title: The upstream's own attribution file, sal063 CREDITS.md, is not present in Nakagawa
findings.detail: sal063 ships CREDITS.md, a detailed third-party attribution document. Nakagawa retains 83.9% of that upstream's code across 44 source files and does not carry the file. NOTICE.md independently covers much of the same substance, so this is not wholesale loss of attribution, but CREDITS.md records specifics NOTICE.md does not: a PINNED PPSSPP REVISION 4e109dd6 for the sceMpeg port; per-file upstream path detail; the claim that recomp.h's CpuState 'VFPU v[128] physical ordering, fpcond/fcr31 split, unaligned LWL/LWR/SWL/SWR, kernel object pool numbering all match PPSSPP'; a warning that the in-code 'faithfulness vs PPSSPP' comments are a language model's assertions rather than an audited fact; and a note that an earlier src/rt/gpu_vk/ bridge 'reused PPSSPP's GPU_Vulkan wholesale' before being removed. That last item is directly relevant to the #102 full-history audit.
findings.action: ADDRESSED 2026-08-06 by IND-6 (#304): the upstream CREDITS.md is now reproduced verbatim at THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES/SAL063_CREDITS.txt, and its specifics were folded into NOTICE.md with attribution to sal063 -- the pinned PPSSPP revision 4e109dd6 for the sceMpeg port, and a lineage statement recording that PPSSPP material reached this project through sal063. The gpu_vk/GPU_Vulkan history question is routed to #102 and remains open there. Qualified human review of the resulting notice presentation is still required before publication. This audit did not and does not assert a license violation.

findings.title: The recompiler pipeline is substantially inherited from sal063 and declares no derivation
findings.detail: This corrects an overclaim in this ledger's own earlier text, which described the pipeline as 'overwhelmingly project-authored'. Measured retention of sal063: tools/codegen.py 83.9% of upstream retained (617 shared lines, 37.5% of the current file), analyze.py 86.2% (280), prxload.py 73.6% (81), imports.py 71.2% (47). None declares any derivation and NOTICE.md has no per-file sal063 inventory. Counting every file with at least 20 shared lines and no header, 3111 shared lines are undeclared at file level, 1481 of them outside nid_names.h. The pipeline is genuinely extended -- codegen more than doubled, and function discovery, chunking, continuation catalogs and the emitter are real additions -- but it began as sal063's and most of sal063's pipeline code is still present.
findings.action: ADDRESSED 2026-08-06 by IND-6: NOTICE.md now carries an 'Upstream source file inventory (sal063-derived modules)' table covering the pipeline and every other measurably inherited file, with the four verified-original tools named explicitly. The file headers were NOT changed; the omission was in NOTICE.md and was fixed by adding to it.

findings.title: Nakagawa standardized PPSSPP source headers, but some upstream attribution already existed in sal063
findings.detail: Of sal063's 44 tracked sources exactly one carries the standardized 'Derived from' header found in Nakagawa: ge_gpu.c. Nakagawa added that header form to ge.c, hle.c, recomp.c/.h, savedata.c, mpeg.c, pgf.c/.h, vfpu_interp.c and evf.h. The earlier wording overreached by calling all per-file PPSSPP attribution a Nakagawa addition: sal063's pgf.c and pgf.h bodies already expressly identify Core/Font/PGF.cpp and a C port, and sal063's CREDITS.md itemizes PGF and several other PPSSPP-derived files. The chain remains PPSSPP -> sal063 -> Nakagawa; source-header standardization and substantive attribution are separate facts.
findings.action: CORRECTED 2026-08-08 in NOTICE.md, this finding, and the independence backlog. Preserve the useful standardized Nakagawa headers without implying that PGF attribution originated in Nakagawa.

findings.title: src/rt/nid_names.h ships eight sentinel identifiers alongside real PSP NIDs
findings.detail: Entries 0x13370001 __IoAsyncFinish, 0xc0de0001-0xc0de0003 __Utility*, 0x756e6e6f / 0x756e6f00 / 0x756e6f10 __Net*Callbacks and 0xdeadbeaf pspeDebugWrite sit in the same lookup table as firmware exports. Their names use the reserved __ prefix and their NID values are sentinels rather than digests; 0xc0de0001-0003 are allocated sequentially across three related names, which a hash cannot produce. The inference that these are emulator-internal identifiers is structural and high-confidence, but it is an inference from numeric shape rather than a proof about PSP firmware. The consequence is a diagnostic-correctness defect: if guest code ever presented one of these NIDs the runtime would name it after emulator internals.
findings.action: Remove the eight, and make the generator incapable of reintroducing sentinel-shaped entries. Do NOT extend the removal to the library-attributed or alias entries, which label real NIDs. Backlog IND-1.
